subject: Throughput & SLO fit — Cinderly dedicated sizing
messages:

Subject: Initial throughput details for dedicated sizing

Hi Sofia —

Good to meet yesterday. Our next step for the Dedicated sizing proposal is a short data check so we can map your expected workload to GPU slabs and recommend a safety buffer. Can you confirm the numbers below (ballpark is fine):

- Typical tokens per response (median / 90th):
- Average requests per minute (or concurrent sessions) at baseline and at peak day:
- Percent of requests that are long-form / streaming vs short completions
- P95 latency target for user-facing calls (ms) and whether you need hard SLOs for p95 or p99
- Any geo preferences (US region required?) and data residency constraints

If you prefer, attach a CSV with a sample request distribution — that works well.

I'll put together a quick model once I have those inputs and share a recommended slab + headroom plan.

Thanks,
Michael Grant

From: Sofia Martinez <sofia@cinderly.ai>

Subject: Re: Initial throughput details for dedicated sizing

Hi Michael —

Thanks — see numbers below and I attached a short CSV (cinderly_token_profile.csv) with a 24-hour sample slice. High level:

- Median tokens per response: 420 tokens
- 90th percentile tokens per response: 1,600 tokens
- Baseline avg requests/minute: 180 RPM (3 RPS)
- Peak concurrent (sustained 10m): ~250 RPS during product scrapes and batch generation spikes
- Long-form / streaming: ~18% of requests; those average 3–5k tokens and use streaming for token-by-token deliver
- P95 latency target (user-facing): 350 ms – we'd like 250 ms if feasible but can accept 350ms for go-live
- Geo: US-only for now; we'll add EU next quarter

Procurement note: procurement@cinderly.ai will expect a 30‑day lead time on dedicated provisioning and a standard contract with SLAs.

Thanks,
Sofia Martinez

Cinderly AI

Subject: Fwd: Initial throughput details for dedicated sizing — preliminary calc and ask

Karthik / Neha —

Looping you in to validate capacity math and the recommended slab plan for Cinderly (see Sofia's numbers above and attached CSV). Quick summary of my back-of-envelope:

Assumptions
- Target model: rw-13b-quant (production q4 variant) — effective serving throughput observed: ~8.5k tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU when serving short-form (inferencing with batch size ~8, 256-context optimistic). For long-form streaming the effective sustained tokens/sec drops to ~5k due to KV cache and IO patterns.
- Baseline avg RPS: 3 RPS -> baseline token/sec = 3 * 420 ≈ 1,260 tps
- Peak concurrent RPS: 250 RPS -> peak token/sec (median sized) = 250 * 420 = 105,000 tps (note: this is an instantaneous burst across requests; most spikes are short and partially batched)
- Long-form impact: 18% of peak requests are long-form averaging 4,000 tokens; those contribute an additional ~0.18 * 250 * (4,000 - 420) ≈ 165,600 extra token work during peak windows

Combined peak token/sec estimate (conservative): ~270k tokens/sec sustained during high-peaks (10m sustained windows).

GPU mapping (rough)
- Effective tokens/sec per GPU (mixed workload): 6k tps (use conservative mixed-workload number)
- GPUs required at peak = 270,000 / 6,000 ≈ 45 GPUs
- Suggested committed slab initial: 60 GPUs (≈ 33% headroom) to cover queuing, warmup, and unexpected model switching.
- Optional burst: allow autoscaling to +20 GPUs for 2x short spikes, or enable routing to hosted fallback model for non-critical workloads.

Latency/SLO fit
- With 60 GPUs and an intelligent batching policy (max latency budget 150ms for batching + 100–200ms model compute), we expect to meet 350ms p95 for short-form. Hitting 250ms p95 would require tighter batching (cost increase) or smaller model variant (rw-7b).

Operational notes
- Recommend prefix cache for repeated prompts (Cinderly has high repetition for templates) — can reduce token cost by ~12–20% and lower effective tps by similar amount.
- Quantized model option (q4f16) reduces per-GPU throughput slightly but allows 25% more concurrency per GPU if you want lower cost.

Attachments: I included a one-page snapshot PDF (redwood_capacity_snapshot.pdf) with an hourly ramp simulation and sensitivity curves.

Questions for Sofia (cc'd)
1) Are your 250 RPS peaks typically spread across multiple regions/clients or concentrated to a few ingest endpoints?
2) Any hard constraints on pricing vs committed GPUs (they mentioned a 30-day lead time — we should map commit tiers)

If Karthik/Neha have alternative numbers (we often show 1.2x–1.5x different GPU efficiency depending on kernel schedule), list them and I will update the estimate.

Thanks,
Michael
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Michael / Karthik / Neha —

Thanks for the detailed breakdown — this is exactly the level we need to move to procurement. A few quick items:

- The peaks are concentrated to two ingestion endpoints (US-West) — so regional placement matters and we'd prefer a US-West slab with fallback to US-East.
- The 250 RPS figure is accurate for our peak windows (10–12 minutes), and spikes are predictable (batch runs).
- We like the 60 GPU recommendation with the 33% headroom. Please include: a price tier for 60 GPUs committed (monthly), an optional 20 GPU burst bundle (on-demand), and a 12‑month vs 36‑month commit discount line.
- Procurement: we need an SLO appendix (p95 latency, uptime SLA, scheduled maintenance windows) and a sample SOC2 attestation.

Next steps: can you send a formal proposal/quote and DocuSign-ready contract with the options above? Procurement is ready to review this week.
